**Title (English, from literature):** Watching entertainment

## AI-generated Overview (from reference literature)

*This overview was drafted by an AI model from the cited scholarship and catalog data and may contain errors; verify against the sources before relying on it.*

Bhikkhunī Vibhaṅga Pācittiya 10 (*Naccagīta*, "Watching entertainment") is a disciplinary rule in the Vinaya Piṭaka concerning Buddhist nuns. The rule stipulates that a nun who goes to see a performance or entertainment show commits an offense that must be confessed. In modern scholarship, Ute Hüsken examines the casuistry and commentary (*Samantapāsādikā*) associated with Bhikkhunī Pācittiya 10, comparing its offenses and grounds for non-offense (*anāpatti*) with corresponding rules governing monks, such as regulations in the Cullavagga prohibiting monastic involvement with dance performances [Hüsken 1997]. Hüsken highlights how the commentary evaluates whether incidental viewing—such as sitting in an assembly hall or turning one's neck while walking on a road—constitutes an offense or an exemption [Hüsken 1997]. An English translation of the rule and its vibhaṅga has been made by Bhikkhu Brahmali.
